notes: Covers respect, dignity, non-harassment, legal compliance, and protection of organizational assets. Reporting mechanism to Director of Human Resources. AWWA is primarily a technical society; professional ethics framing is lighter than sector-specific bodies.

Standards for honesty of credentials representation, proper product application, marketing accuracy, and public protection. Certification revocation is the enforcement mechanism. Includes marketing guidelines to prevent consumer deception about water quality.

Covers integrity, honesty, professional excellence, collaboration, legal compliance, and accountability. Members align with Engineering Council and Royal Academy of Engineering ethical principles. Commitment made at joining and at every membership renewal.

organization: Chartered Institution of Water and Environmental Management
document_title: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
notes: Mandatory for Chartered Water and Environmental Manager (CWEM) status. Members must demonstrate awareness of compliance with the Code. CIWEM runs professional ethics CPD events and maintains an ethics complaint mechanism. Applies to both water (Div 36) and environmental management (Div 39).

Addresses three categories of misconduct: Personal, Professional, and Legal. Requires civility, ethical business conduct, diversity/equity/inclusion support. Supplemented by Event Code of Conduct and Member Association Code of Conduct Toolkit. WEF also maintains standards for water environment professionals through its WEF Sets the Standard program.

Required to be signed before certification application can proceed. Covers legal compliance, honest competition, industry integrity, and faithful professional representation. Focused on decentralized/onsite sewage systems.

organization: Solid Waste Association of North America
notes: Code of Ethics must be signed before a certification application can begin. SWANA certification covers solid waste managers, operators, and technicians. Separate Code of Conduct available via member community portal.

document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice for Environmental Professionals
notes: One of the most comprehensive ethics codes for environmental professionals. Broad view of environment (physical, natural, cultural). Covers data validity responsibility, conflict of interest disclosure, public fidelity, employer loyalty, and non-condoning of misrepresentation. Applies to EIA, remediation, environmental planning professionals.

organization: Society of Environmental Toxicology and Chemistry
notes: Applies to governance members, employees, members, volunteers, and guests. Principles include scientific integrity, intellectual property respect, avoiding misleading statements, confidentiality, and minimizing environmental effects of research. Supplemented by a separate Code of Conduct.

Members compile/review impact assessments with integrity and impartiality. Covers equity considerations, Indigenous peoples' rights, future generations, and non-advancement of private interests to the public detriment. Also provides FasTips: Ethics and Best Practice Principles of EIA guidance documents.

organization: Virginia Section AWWA / Water Works Professionals
document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice for Water Works Professionals
notes: State-level AWWA section code of ethics for water works professionals. Cited as a representative example of state-section professional ethics codes that supplement AWWA national Code of Practice.
